items.title: Quincy Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I’ve been living with them. They’re like my family... Hilary stays at my house. I love Obama. I really do... I’m with Hilary and Bill.

ctx.x: Let me ask then about again, because you were out there when Monk [Montgomery] began playing the Fender bass for the first time. That opened up another whole avenue, James Jamison and all those people. Can you tell us anything about what was going at the beginning of this?

Yes. What happened was, in 1999, on one of the covers of USA Today – you can check it out – I picked it up one day, and there was a painting of a lady, Steve Case, Bill Gates, and myself. I said, what the hell is that? I’d done an interview, but I didn’t know what it was for, with USA Today. It was about what single piece of technology affected your genre the heaviest. I automatically said the Fender bass . . .
